title: Review: next_delivery() for per-user quiet hours
claimed_change:
Add notify/schedule.py with next_delivery(now, tz, quiet) -> datetime.
- now is an aware datetime (ValueError if naive); tz is a tzinfo such as notify.tz.EASTERN; quiet is a notify.quiet.QuietHours.
- If the user's local time at now is outside quiet hours, return now converted to UTC.
- Otherwise return, as an aware UTC datetime, the first instant after now at which the user's local wall clock reads quiet.end. This must hold across daylight-saving changes: with quiet hours 22:00-07:00, a notification created the evening before a DST switch goes out at 07:00 local time on the user's clock the next morning.
- Quiet-hour boundaries never fall inside the 01:00-03:00 transition window.
- Add tests.

ground_truth.description: next_delivery returns now + (release - local). Both operands share the same tzinfo, so Python subtracts them as naive wall-clock times and ignores the UTC offset change; on a DST-transition night the result is one hour off (06:00 EST instead of 07:00 after fall-back, 08:00 EDT after spring-forward). Fix: return release.astimezone(timezone.utc).
